entity.name: uart_spi_protocol_bridge_top
entity.description: Design a UART-to-SPI protocol bridge with transmit and receive FIFOs that cleanly accepts UART traffic, frames transactions, and drives an SPI master path with explicit status/error reporting.

behavior: Design a UART-to-SPI protocol bridge with transmit and receive FIFOs that cleanly accepts UART traffic, frames transactions, and drives an SPI master path with explicit status/error reporting.
Required block/responsibility: uart_rx receiver path
Required block/responsibility: uart_tx transmitter path
Required block/responsibility: spi_master controller
Required block/responsibility: tx_fifo buffering for outbound SPI payloads
Required block/responsibility: rx_fifo buffering for inbound SPI response data
Required block/responsibility: control/status register block or equivalent status signaling
Required block/responsibility: bridge control FSM coordinating UART framing and SPI execution
Required block/responsibility: error reporting for framing, overflow, underflow, and protocol faults
Keep UART framing logic separate from SPI transaction execution logic.
Make FIFO widths, depths, and framing assumptions explicit with generics or constants where practical.
Use explicit state-machine transitions for idle, load, transmit, receive, and error recovery behavior.
Prefer a single synchronous clock domain unless another domain is absolutely justified and documented.
Reset behavior must be deterministic and compatible with the selected reset style in the app.
Do not use gated clocks; use clock-enable style control instead.
corner_cases: Exercise nominal transfers from UART into SPI and back again.
Exercise FIFO backpressure, framing errors, overflow/underflow handling, and representative recovery behavior.
Produce deterministic PASS/FAIL assertions with useful messages.
prohibited_implementations: Do not collapse the entire design into one monolithic process without architectural structure.
Do not omit FIFOs or replace them with hand-wavy placeholder comments.
Do not claim protocol behavior that is not represented in the RTL or testbench.
synthesis_requirements: All generated VHDL must compile with GHDL using VHDL-2008.
The bridge must elaborate and simulate successfully under GHDL.
The testbench must prove nominal transfers and at least one error-path scenario.
The generated project must include clear top-level ownership of UART, SPI, buffering, and control responsibilities.
testbench_obligations: Exercise nominal transfers from UART into SPI and back again.
Exercise FIFO backpressure, framing errors, overflow/underflow handling, and representative recovery behavior.
Produce deterministic PASS/FAIL assertions with useful messages.

entity.name: axi_stream_packet_router_top
entity.description: Design an AXI-Stream packet router or small network-switch style fabric in VHDL with scalable routing, deterministic arbitration, and verifiable valid/ready handshake behavior.

behavior: Design an AXI-Stream packet router or small network-switch style fabric in VHDL with scalable routing, deterministic arbitration, and verifiable valid/ready handshake behavior.
Required block/responsibility: AXI-Stream source/sink interface handling
Required block/responsibility: routing decision logic
Required block/responsibility: arbitration logic for contended outputs
Required block/responsibility: backpressure handling
Required block/responsibility: packet or frame tracking support as needed by the architecture
Required block/responsibility: top-level scalable switch/router integration
Make arbitration policy explicit.
Backpressure behavior must be deterministic and represented in the RTL.
Scalability should come from clean structure or generics, not copied ad hoc logic.
Use a single deterministic streaming clock domain unless an alternative is explicitly justified.
Reset must place all handshake/control state into a known idle condition.
Handshake behavior must never depend on gated clocks or hidden latches.
corner_cases: Cover handshake correctness, contention, routing correctness, and backpressure scenarios.
Include representative packet-flow cases and deterministic pass/fail checks.
prohibited_implementations: Do not claim AXI-Stream compatibility while omitting valid/ready semantics.
Do not ignore backpressure or contention handling.
Do not flatten a scalable switch into undocumented one-off wiring.
synthesis_requirements: Generated RTL and verification files must compile, elaborate, and simulate under GHDL.
The testbench must demonstrate correct valid/ready behavior under both nominal and contended cases.
The architecture must show a credible routing and arbitration structure.
testbench_obligations: Cover handshake correctness, contention, routing correctness, and backpressure scenarios.
Include representative packet-flow cases and deterministic pass/fail checks.

entity.name: dsp_chain_top
entity.description: Design a DSP processing chain in VHDL consisting of a FIR filter followed by an FFT-lite or spectral analyzer stage, with explicit signed or fixed-point arithmetic and verifiable pipeline latency.

behavior: Design a DSP processing chain in VHDL consisting of a FIR filter followed by an FFT-lite or spectral analyzer stage, with explicit signed or fixed-point arithmetic and verifiable pipeline latency.
Required block/responsibility: sample input staging path
Required block/responsibility: FIR filter datapath with explicit coefficients or coefficient placeholders
Required block/responsibility: pipeline registers and latency bookkeeping
Required block/responsibility: FFT-lite or spectral-analysis stage
Required block/responsibility: output-valid or result-ready signaling
Required block/responsibility: top-level DSP chain integration
Use signed or fixed-point arithmetic explicitly; do not rely on ambiguous implicit typing.
Document widths, growth, truncation, rounding, and saturation assumptions.
Keep stage-to-stage latency visible in the architecture and in the verification plan.
Use a deterministic synchronous pipeline model.
Reset must put all pipeline state into known values.
Latency through the datapath must be explicit and testable.
corner_cases: Generate a self-checking testbench aware of pipeline latency.
Verify representative numeric behavior through the FIR stage and the analyzer stage.
Check latency alignment between input stimulus and observed output results.
prohibited_implementations: Do not omit explicit numeric types and width handling.
Do not produce a DSP chain with undocumented latency.
Do not replace the analyzer stage with placeholder comments while claiming completion.
synthesis_requirements: All generated VHDL must compile, elaborate, and simulate under GHDL.
The testbench must demonstrate deterministic latency-aware checking.
The generated design must show a clear staged architecture rather than a vague arithmetic sketch.
testbench_obligations: Generate a self-checking testbench aware of pipeline latency.
Verify representative numeric behavior through the FIR stage and the analyzer stage.
Check latency alignment between input stimulus and observed output results.

entity.name: video_pattern_generator_top
entity.description: Design a VGA or HDMI-style pattern generator with a framebuffer-oriented architecture in VHDL, including deterministic sync timing, pixel addressing, and a verifiable top-level video path.

behavior: Design a VGA or HDMI-style pattern generator with a framebuffer-oriented architecture in VHDL, including deterministic sync timing, pixel addressing, and a verifiable top-level video path.
Required block/responsibility: horizontal timing counter
Required block/responsibility: vertical timing counter
Required block/responsibility: sync generation logic
Required block/responsibility: active-video window generation
Required block/responsibility: framebuffer or framebuffer-style pixel addressing path
Required block/responsibility: pattern generator or pixel formatting stage
Required block/responsibility: top-level video output integration
Keep timing generation separate from pixel/pattern generation.
Make video timing assumptions explicit instead of implied.
Address generation must be internally consistent with active video dimensions.
Use a deterministic single pixel-domain clock model unless more are explicitly justified.
Reset must place timing counters and sync outputs into a known state.
Timing constants must be explicit and easy to review.
corner_cases: Verify timing windows, sync pulse widths, counter wrap behavior, and representative pixel flow.
Use deterministic checks rather than visual-only inspection.
prohibited_implementations: Do not hand-wave timing with comments while omitting real counters and sync logic.
Do not mix all timing and pixel behavior into unreadable combinational logic.
Do not generate a video design with no explicit sync behavior.
synthesis_requirements: Generated VHDL must compile, elaborate, and simulate under GHDL.
The testbench must verify sync timing behavior and at least one representative pixel-addressing scenario.
The architecture must clearly separate timing generation from pixel data generation.
testbench_obligations: Verify timing windows, sync pulse widths, counter wrap behavior, and representative pixel flow.
Use deterministic checks rather than visual-only inspection.

entity.description: Design a small CPU core project in VHDL, choosing either a mini RISC-V subset or a coherent custom 8-bit ISA, with a complete fetch/decode/execute path and deterministic verification.

behavior: Design a small CPU core project in VHDL, choosing either a mini RISC-V subset or a coherent custom 8-bit ISA, with a complete fetch/decode/execute path and deterministic verification.
Required block/responsibility: instruction fetch path with program counter management
Required block/responsibility: instruction decoder
Required block/responsibility: ALU with clearly defined supported operations
Required block/responsibility: register file
Required block/responsibility: control unit or control FSM
Required block/responsibility: program memory interface
Required block/responsibility: data memory interface
Required block/responsibility: branch/jump or control-flow handling
Required block/responsibility: top-level CPU integration entity
State the chosen ISA subset or custom instruction set clearly.
Define operand widths, register count, and memory interface semantics explicitly.
Keep decode, execute, and state-update behavior understandable rather than opaque.
Assume a single clock domain for the core and document any alternative choice explicitly.
Reset must place the CPU into a deterministic fetch-ready state.
Avoid gated clocks and uncontrolled combinational feedback between control and datapath blocks.
corner_cases: The testbench must prove fetch, decode, execute, register update, and control-flow behavior with deterministic checks.
Include representative arithmetic, logical, load/store, and branch-style scenarios where supported by the chosen ISA.
prohibited_implementations: Do not describe the CPU as complete while omitting decode or write-back behavior.
Do not use placeholder pseudo-instructions without implementing them in the RTL and testbench.
Do not hide the memory interface behind undocumented magic constants or comments.
synthesis_requirements: Generated RTL and testbench must compile, elaborate, and simulate under GHDL.
The testbench must verify successful execution of a short deterministic instruction sequence.
The generated collateral must make the architectural split between datapath and control clear.
testbench_obligations: The testbench must prove fetch, decode, execute, register update, and control-flow behavior with deterministic checks.
Include representative arithmetic, logical, load/store, and branch-style scenarios where supported by the chosen ISA.
